title: AI or not?
instruction: Does it learn from data and make guesses? Then it's AI. Does it just follow exact rules? Then it isn't.

items.why: It learns from what you watch and guesses what will keep you there.
A fixed rule: ring at 7:00. It learns nothing.
A model learned to turn speech into text from a huge number of recordings.
Adding is an exact procedure. The result isn't guessed, it's calculated.

items.text: You unlock your phone with your face
items.why: A model learned to recognise your face even in different light or with glasses.
A timer with a fixed rule. Traffic lights that learn from the traffic would be AI.
It learned from millions of translated sentences how a sentence is most likely translated.

items.text: A lift goes to the floor you chose
items.why: You press 3 and it goes to floor 3. An exact rule, no learning.
A language model guesses the next words from what it learned from texts.

debrief: You can tell AI by the fact that it learned from examples and makes guesses. A program with fixed rules only does what someone wrote for it exactly, even if it looks clever.
